title: Sabo (Talwandi) Region A Talwandi of Brars (Talwandi of Rai Dalla, Expulsion of An Ogre from Bhatinda)

blocks.text: Then Satguru thought that behind this latest Mughal invasion, There was the conspiracy of Nawab Kapoora of Kot Kapoora. So leaving Jallanwal4 cluster of Brar villages, The Guru arrived safe and sound at Talwandi Sabo. (1)
lines: Then Satguru thought that behind this latest Mughal invasion,
There was the conspiracy of Nawab Kapoora of Kot Kapoora.
So leaving Jallanwal4 cluster of Brar villages,
The Guru arrived safe and sound at Talwandi Sabo.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thus after heading towards Talwandi Sabo of Rai Dalla, The Guru finally arrived and stayed at Talwandi Sabo. Imploring the Guru to get rid of the mercenary Brars, Rai Dalla requested the Guru to be his guest of honour. (2)
lines: Thus after heading towards Talwandi Sabo of Rai Dalla,
The Guru finally arrived and stayed at Talwandi Sabo.
Imploring the Guru to get rid of the mercenary Brars,
Rai Dalla requested the Guru to be his guest of honour.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Rai Dalla implored the Guru to accompany him to his seat, And assured the Guru of his whole-hearted support. He would neither desert the Guru through thick and thin, Nor would he charge any wages for his services (like the Brars). (3)
lines: Rai Dalla implored the Guru to accompany him to his seat,
And assured the Guru of his whole-hearted support.
He would neither desert the Guru through thick and thin,
Nor would he charge any wages for his services (like the Brars).

blocks.text: Chaupai:

On the contrary, Rai Dalla would serve the Guru to the best of his resources, He would offer everything in cash, kind and services to the Guru. He summoned all the members of his family into Guru's presence; And they all paid obeisance to the Guru as per Rai's instructions. (4)
lines: On the contrary,
Rai Dalla would serve the Guru to the best of his resources,
He would offer everything in cash, kind and services to the Guru.
He summoned all the members of his family into Guru's presence;
And they all paid obeisance to the Guru as per Rai's instructions.

blocks.text: While someone made offerings of gold coins or one-rupee coins and clothings, Others made offerings of cows, buffaloes, horses and diverse other things. Someone offered food grains for running a community kitchen, While others made offerings of butter oil and salt ingredients. (5)
lines: While someone made offerings of gold coins or one-rupee coins and clothings,
Others made offerings of cows, buffaloes, horses and diverse other things.
Someone offered food grains for running a community kitchen,
While others made offerings of butter oil and salt ingredients.

blocks.text: Rai Dalla sent messengers through out his entire territory, Lest they might be overtaken by a sudden Mughal invasion. He informed his subjects to assemble on a minute's notice, Instead of keeping asleep at home like Kapoora's subjects. (6)
lines: Rai Dalla sent messengers through out his entire territory,
Lest they might be overtaken by a sudden Mughal invasion.
He informed his subjects to assemble on a minute's notice,
Instead of keeping asleep at home like Kapoora's subjects.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Satguru showered his blessings on Rai Dalla and his subjects, As all the inhabitants of this forested terrain paid obeisance to the Guru. All inhabitants visited the Guru with their humble offerings, And returned with the manifold blessings of the Guru. (7)
lines: Satguru showered his blessings on Rai Dalla and his subjects,
As all the inhabitants of this forested terrain paid obeisance to the Guru.
All inhabitants visited the Guru with their humble offerings,
And returned with the manifold blessings of the Guru.

blocks.text: Chaupai One day, a large congregation of the Sikhs arrived at Talwandi, And they approached the Guru with the following words:
"Guruji, it is an established truth that Jats are loud mouthed, As their mouths have been opened by the pick of an axe by the Divine." (8)
lines: "Guruji, it is an established truth that Jats are loud mouthed,
As their mouths have been opened by the pick of an axe by the Divine."

blocks.text: They pleaded forcefully before the Guru for succour, Because how could adversity prevail in the presence of the Guru. They asserted that although they worked extremely hard in their fields, Yet they always remained indigent and in want of necessities. (9)
lines: They pleaded forcefully before the Guru for succour,
Because how could adversity prevail in the presence of the Guru.
They asserted that although they worked extremely hard in their fields,
Yet they always remained indigent and in want of necessities.

blocks.text: They disclosed that there lived an ogre at Bathinda, Who always devoured all what they produced. After listening to their woes, Satguru called for Rai Dalla, And initiated him as a Singh after administering amrit. (10)
lines: They disclosed that there lived an ogre at Bathinda,
Who always devoured all what they produced.
After listening to their woes,
Satguru called for Rai Dalla,
And initiated him as a Singh after administering amrit.

blocks.text: The Guru asked him to lead him to the town of Bathinda, So that he may provide succour to the people by expelling the ogre. Rai Dalla Singh, obeying the orders of the revered Guru, Led the Guru to Bathinda and stayed put there with the Guru. (11)
lines: The Guru asked him to lead him to the town of Bathinda,
So that he may provide succour to the people by expelling the ogre.
Rai Dalla Singh, obeying the orders of the revered Guru,
Led the Guru to Bathinda and stayed put there with the Guru.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The Guru put up a camp at Bathinda to deal with the ogre, As the ogre also came down to assess the newly arrived Guru. He caused a fierce hailstorm and darkening wind to blow, In order to harass, frighten and disperse the general populace. (12)
lines: The Guru put up a camp at Bathinda to deal with the ogre,
As the ogre also came down to assess the newly arrived Guru.
He caused a fierce hailstorm and darkening wind to blow,
In order to harass, frighten and disperse the general populace.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

He caused some people to be stricken with fever and nausea, While some others were induced to stammer in a delirium. The haunted people started complaining on behalf of the ogre, That he (the ogre) had been residing at Bathinda for a long time. (13)
lines: He caused some people to be stricken with fever and nausea,
While some others were induced to stammer in a delirium.
The haunted people started complaining on behalf of the ogre,
That he (the ogre) had been residing at Bathinda for a long time.

blocks.text: Satguru told the ogre that since the people of Bathinda were Guru's followers, The ogre must vacate this place and shift to some other place. Otherwise he would be done to death for his disobedience, By handing him over to be tortured by the spirits of Singh Martyrs. (14)
lines: Satguru told the ogre that since the people of Bathinda were Guru's followers,
The ogre must vacate this place and shift to some other place.
Otherwise he would be done to death for his disobedience,
By handing him over to be tortured by the spirits of Singh Martyrs.

blocks.text: The Guru imprisoned his evil spirit in the body of a human being, Who was severely tortured by handcuffing his hands and legs. The Guru threatened to kill him by burning him in hell fire, Along with his whole progeny of his sons and grandsons. (15)
lines: The Guru imprisoned his evil spirit in the body of a human being,
Who was severely tortured by handcuffing his hands and legs.
The Guru threatened to kill him by burning him in hell fire,
Along with his whole progeny of his sons and grandsons.

blocks.text: The ogre revealed that he was a brother of another ogre Makho5 , And pleaded that he might kindly be sent to join his brother. Or the Guru should accept him also into the Sikh fold, And assured the Guru of his whole-hearted allegiance and service. (16)
lines: The ogre revealed that he was a brother of another ogre Makho5 ,
And pleaded that he might kindly be sent to join his brother.
Or the Guru should accept him also into the Sikh fold,
And assured the Guru of his whole-hearted allegiance and service.

blocks.text: Then Satguru ordered him to leave Bathinda forever, And establish himself in the town of Sirhind. The Guru instructed him to wreck the foundations of the Sirhind empire, And devour all those who tried to defend the Sirhind rulers. (17)
lines: Then Satguru ordered him to leave Bathinda forever,
And establish himself in the town of Sirhind.
The Guru instructed him to wreck the foundations of the Sirhind empire,
And devour all those who tried to defend the Sirhind rulers.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The ogre left Bathinda after paying obeisance to the Guru, And went on his way to the Mughal town of Sirhind. Rai Dalla, then, beseached Satguru after the ogre's departure, That they should make a sacrifice of a Buffalo to the Goddess Bhawani. (18)
lines: The ogre left Bathinda after paying obeisance to the Guru,
And went on his way to the Mughal town of Sirhind.
Rai Dalla, then, beseached Satguru after the ogre's departure,
That they should make a sacrifice of a Buffalo to the Goddess Bhawani.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereupon, the Guru asked Rai Dalla for a buffalo to be brought, Whose blood was sprinkled around the fort after its slaughter. After that the Guru made this fort as his camp site, There was plenty and prosperity in the whole Malwa region. (19)
lines: Thereupon, the Guru asked Rai Dalla for a buffalo to be brought,
Whose blood was sprinkled around the fort after its slaughter.
After that the Guru made this fort as his camp site,
There was plenty and prosperity in the whole Malwa region.

blocks.text: S. Dyal Singh and Fateh Singh from village Bhai ka Chhak came, And were initiated after taking Pahul6 from the Guru. Then came the grandsons of Bhai Rupa, a carpenter, They were S. Param Singh, Karam Singh who received Pahul from the Guru. (20)
lines: S.
Dyal Singh and Fateh Singh from village Bhai ka Chhak came,
And were initiated after taking Pahul6 from the Guru.
Then came the grandsons of Bhai Rupa, a carpenter,
They were S.
Param Singh,
Karam Singh who received Pahul from the Guru.

blocks.text: The Guru sent a message to Sodhi Kaul7 to his native place, Who brought Abhey Ram's son with him from amongst his family. The Guru showered his blessings on this devout Sikh, And kept him in his company after initiating him with Pahul. (21)
lines: The Guru sent a message to Sodhi Kaul7 to his native place,
Who brought Abhey Ram's son with him from amongst his family.
The Guru showered his blessings on this devout Sikh,
And kept him in his company after initiating him with Pahul.

blocks.text: Then the Guru made a remark about the person of Sodhi Kaul, That he seemed to be worthy of Guru's trust. Sodhi Kaul was instructed to stay with the Guru, Who always made an obeisance to the Guru every morning. (22)
lines: Then the Guru made a remark about the person of Sodhi Kaul,
That he seemed to be worthy of Guru's trust.
Sodhi Kaul was instructed to stay with the Guru,
Who always made an obeisance to the Guru every morning.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Then Satguru camped at Damdama (Talwandi Sabo) after Bathinda, Where he kept on sharpening quills and throwing those out and, Remarking that this place would be Guru's seat of learning, Where the ignorant would receive knowledge and enlightenment. (23)
lines: Then Satguru camped at Damdama (Talwandi Sabo) after Bathinda,
Where he kept on sharpening quills and throwing those out and,
Remarking that this place would be Guru's seat of learning,
Where the ignorant would receive knowledge and enlightenment.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The inhabitants of the town of Meharaj also came to the Guru, And they made offerings of milch cattle, horses and one tenth of their earnings. Both the sons of Sodhi Kaul also got initiated as Singhs, And they came to be called Ram Singh and Tarlok Singh. (24)
lines: The inhabitants of the town of Meharaj also came to the Guru,
And they made offerings of milch cattle, horses and one tenth of their earnings.
Both the sons of Sodhi Kaul also got initiated as Singhs,
And they came to be called Ram Singh and Tarlok Singh.
